newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Aegis sees Europe market improving.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Aegis sees Europe market improving.

text.p: Aegis Group Plc, parent company of the Carat media planning and buying network, expects growth in display advertising in Europe to rise to five to six percent in 1997 from four percent this year, chief executive Crispin Davis said on Tuesday.
"I would expect over the next 18 months we would see a slight strengthening," Davis told Reuters in an interview following the release of first-half results.
Aegis had forecast six percent growth in the European display advertising market earlier this year, but now expects only four percent growth in 1996.
"I think the four percent rather than the six percent reflects slightly sluggish economic growth, particularly in Germany," Davis said. "The rest of Europe is pretty much as we anticipated."
The UK and France were particularly strong markets for Aegis in the 1996 first half, with each posting double digit growth.
"As far as we're concerned we were able to deliver a pretty good set of results despite an average market," Davis said.
Aegis's pretax profits rose 15 percent to 18.7 million stg in the 1996 first half from 16.3 million a year ago. Turnover rose eight percent to 1.81 billion stg from 1.67 billion.
Davis said gross margins improved for the first time in several years, rising to 4.9 percent from 4.8 percent. Operating margins rose to 24 percent.
Aegis is experiencing strong growth in Eastern Europe, a market it entered three years ago.

"The market is growing very fast, between 20 and 30 percent, and we are gaining share in these markets very rapidly," Davis said. Aegis' own operations in Eastern Europe are growing at 30 to 50 percent. "Poland and the Czech Republic are performing very well," Davis said. "We would now estimate in Eastern Europe we are in the top five."

Eastern Europe remains a small part of Aegis' total business, accounting for less than five percent of the total. "But over the next few years we see it becoming quite significant," Davis said. "I think five years from now Eastern Europe will be more than 10 percent of our European business."

Aegis is also moving into the U.S. market for the first time, with acquisition of New York-based Media Buying Services International. The company, which had been privately owned, has annual billings of about $160 million.
Davis said Aegis paid about $5 million at a price/earnings ratio of about 10 times.
But the increasing complexity and fragmentation of the media market is raising the need for specialists to help companies maximise their advertising spend.
"These advertisers are looking for much more sophisticated kind of help," Davis said.

The growing number of television channels, the proliferation of magazines, increasing numbers of radio stations, as well as the advent of the Internet and home shopping is increasing the need for specialist media buying services.

Davis said Aegis plans to use Media Buying Services as its initial foothold in the U.S. market and aims to grow the business organically. "But I wouldn't rule out other acquisitions if something suitable came up," he said.
Aegis' shares were off one-half pence at 65p on volume on 930,883.
